english: Let $L$ be the line $\dfrac{2x-1}{3}=\dfrac{3y+1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{-4}$. Then the number of points on $L$ whose coordinates are all integers and whose $z$-coordinate satisfies $|z|\le 500$ is ______.
hindi: माना $L$ रेखा $\dfrac{2x-1}{3}=\dfrac{3y+1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{-4}$ है। तब $L$ पर स्थित उन बिन्दुओं की संख्या, जिनके सभी निर्देशांक पूर्णांक हैं तथा जिनका $z$-निर्देशांक $|z|\le 500$ को सन्तुष्ट करता है, ______ है।
solution_full: Put each ratio equal to $t$: $2x-1=3t$, $3y+1=2t$, $z-2=-4t$, so $x=\dfrac{1+3t}{2}$, $y=\dfrac{2t-1}{3}$, $z=2-4t$ (parametric form of $L$; it passes through $\left(\dfrac12,-\dfrac13,2\right)$ with direction ratios $\dfrac32,\dfrac23,-4$).
If $x$ and $y$ are integers then $3t=2x-1$ and $2t=3y+1$ are integers, so $t=3t-2t$ is an integer; then $z=2-4t$ is automatically an integer.
For integer $t$: $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ requires $1+3t$ even, that is $t$ odd; $y\in\mathbb{Z}$ requires $3\mid 2t-1$, that is $t\equiv2\pmod3$.
Then $x=\dfrac{16+18k}{2}=9k+8$, $y=\dfrac{12k+9}{3}=4k+3$, $z=2-24k-20=-24k-18$; every integer $k$ gives an integer point, and distinct $k$ give distinct points.
So $k=-21,-20,\ldots,20$: that is $42$ values (end checks: $k=-21$ gives $z=486$, $k=20$ gives $z=-498$, $k=-22$ gives $z=510$, $k=21$ gives $z=-522$).
originality_note: New: lattice points on a space line whose symmetric equation has coefficients on x and y, so the integrality of all coordinates becomes a pair of congruences on the parameter (way 5, linking the line equation with integrality). Closest known: 'number of integer points on a segment in the plane' (gcd count). Different because: the line is not given through a lattice point with integer direction ratios; the solver must convert the form and solve t odd, t = 2 mod 3.

concept_use.Equation of a line: Reading the symmetric (Cartesian) equation with coefficients on x and y: point (1/2, -1/3, 2) and direction ratios 3/2, 2/3, -4.
concept_use.Parametric form of a line: Parametric form x = (1+3t)/2, y = (2t-1)/3, z = 2-4t, used to turn integrality into conditions on t and to count the parameters with |z| <= 500.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, vector and point is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated 'coordinates are all integers' and the bound only on z, so the count is finite and unique; checked the end values k = -21 and k = 20 and that k = -22, 21 fail. Changed: No change.
key_step: Showing t must be an integer and solving t odd, t = 2 (mod 3) to get the lattice points (9k+8, 4k+3, -24k-18).
justification: Two ideas linked: converting a non-standard symmetric form to parametric form, and a congruence argument with an end-point count where a slip changes the answer. Numerical; comparable in demand to the bounded counting of 2026-P1-Q11 (L3).
